rationale:
The site is the bundled skill `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`. It has front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions`.

The requirement has one MUST: the description states when to use the skill, in terms of the user's task. The front-matter description opens with "Use when adopting Habeas in an existing codebase", then "when the user asks for a requirements coverage audit". Both are user tasks. It adds a symptom trigger, `habeas status` warning about uncovered items across most of a project's code. That is an observable situation in the user's work, so it does not detract from the task framing.

The description ends with "For a few uncovered items, use habeas-evidence." The requirement allows this with MAY, since it permits naming another bundled skill where an agent could confuse the two. The two skills are easy to confuse, so the pointer is reasonable.

No violation queries matched, and I found no gap.
